questions.q: Your group project has one member who isn't doing their share. What's the best first step?
o: Talk to them privately and ask what's getting in the way
Do their part yourself so the project is good, and complain about it later
Tell the teacher immediately without speaking to them
Remove their name from the project
questions.why: A private conversation can reveal a problem you can solve together.

questions.q: You're new to a class where everyone already has friends. What's a good way to fit in?
o: Join a club or activity where you share interests
Wait quietly until someone invites you to sit with them
Act like you don't need friends
questions.why: Shared interests are an easy way to make friends.

questions.q: Two friends ask you to choose sides in their fight. What's best?
o: Stay neutral and encourage them to talk to each other
Choose the friend you have known longer, because loyalty matters
Tell each one what the other said
questions.why: Staying neutral helps you keep both friendships and helps them sort it out.

questions.q: In a group discussion, one person keeps talking over others. As a leader, what do you do?
o: Politely say, "Let's hear from everyone," and invite others in
Let them keep talking since they seem to have the most ideas
Tell them to be quiet in front of all
questions.why: Fair leaders make space for every voice.

questions.q: You disagree with your teammate's plan for the science fair. What's a respectful approach?
o: Say what you like about it, then suggest your change with reasons
Go along with it to avoid an argument, and complain to others later
questions.why: Starting with what you like makes people open to suggestions.

questions.q: A classmate from another state is teased for their accent. What should you do?
o: Support them and tell the teasers it's not okay
Laugh along a little so the teasers don't start on you next
Advise them to change their accent
questions.why: Standing up for others builds a respectful class.

questions.q: You're the captain and your team lost. What should you say to the team?
o: "We played hard. Let's learn and improve for next time."
"We lost because a few people didn't try hard enough today."
"I don't want to talk about it."
questions.why: A good captain lifts the team and focuses on improvement.

questions.q: Your friend shares something private with you. What should you do?
o: Keep it private unless someone could get hurt
Tell only your best friend, because they never tell anyone
Use it in a joke later
questions.why: Keeping confidences builds trust, except when safety is at risk.

questions.q: You see someone sitting alone at the canteen. What can you do?
o: Invite them to join your table
Wait for them to come over if they want company
Assume they want to be alone
questions.why: Small invitations help others feel included.

questions.q: Your team has to choose a project topic but everyone wants different ones. What's fair?
o: List the ideas and vote, or combine the best ones
Let the loudest person decide so the group doesn't waste time
questions.why: Voting or combining ideas is a fair way for a group to decide.

questions.q: A friend borrowed money and hasn't returned it. What's best?
o: Remind them politely and ask when they can pay
Tell everyone in class that they don't pay people back
questions.why: A polite reminder respects the friendship.

questions.q: You notice your classmate is struggling with English. How can you help?
o: Speak to them only in English slowly
questions.why: Practising together builds skill and friendship.

questions.q: You've been asked to plan a class party. How do you include everyone?
o: Ask classmates for ideas about food, games and music
Invite only your friends to plan
Keep it a secret surprise and plan everything by yourself
questions.why: Asking for ideas makes everyone feel part of it.

questions.q: Your friend is upset because you didn't reply to their message. What's best?
o: Apologise and explain you got busy
Say you don't have to reply
Make up an excuse about your phone battery dying
questions.why: Honest explanations keep trust.

questions.q: A teacher asks a question and a shy classmate gives a wrong answer. Others laugh. What can you do?
o: Not laugh, and say something encouraging later
Correct them loudly so everyone learns the right answer
questions.why: Encouragement helps shy classmates keep trying.

questions.q: In a team game, your friend wants to play but isn't very good. What's the best approach?
o: Include them and help them improve
Let them play only when winning
Tell them to practise on their own first and join later
questions.why: Including friends and helping them is good team spirit.

questions.q: You disagree with a rule your friends made in a game. What do you do?
o: Explain your reason and suggest a fair change
Ignore the rule quietly and keep playing your own way
questions.why: Suggesting changes calmly helps the group agree.

questions.q: Your friend says something rude to your sibling. What's best?
o: Tell your friend calmly that it isn't okay
Never talk to your friend again and tell your sibling to avoid them
questions.why: Calmly standing up for family shows respect.

questions.q: You're in a group chat where people are being mean about someone. What do you do?
o: Say it isn't kind and stop it there
Join in with a joke so the group doesn't turn on you next
questions.why: Speaking up can stop online meanness.

questions.q: Your team won because of someone else's great play. What's right?
o: Give them credit in front of everyone
Accept the praise as captain and say nothing about their play
questions.why: Giving credit openly is fair and builds team spirit.

questions.q: You need help with homework but feel embarrassed to ask. What's best?
o: Ask a friend or teacher politely
Pretend you understand and hope it comes clear later
questions.why: Asking for help is smart and normal.

questions.q: A friend is always late to group meetings. What's a good way to handle it?
o: Agree on a time together and send a reminder
Tell the teacher every time they are late, without speaking to them first
questions.why: Agreeing on times and reminders solves the problem kindly.

questions.q: You see a classmate drop money without noticing. What should you do?
o: Pick it up and give it back
Keep it if no one saw
Give it to the teacher at the end of term
Tell others to look for it
questions.why: Returning things is honest and builds trust.

questions.q: Your friend has different beliefs and festivals from yours. What's respectful?
o: Learn about their festivals and wish them
Ask them to celebrate your festivals instead, so you share more
questions.why: Learning about others' traditions builds respect.

questions.q: You're leading a group and one member's idea is weak. What's a kind response?
o: Thank them and ask how it could be improved
Ignore the idea politely and move on to the next one
questions.why: Valuing every idea keeps people contributing.

questions.q: Your friends want to prank a teacher. You don't feel okay. What do you do?
o: Say you're not comfortable and suggest something else
Tell the teacher secretly so your friends get caught in the act
questions.why: Saying no politely shows respect and courage.

questions.q: You are on a team where people speak different home languages. How do you communicate well?
o: Use simple shared words and check everyone understood
Let only the best speakers talk so the work gets done quickly
questions.why: Checking understanding helps everyone take part.

questions.q: A classmate keeps copying your work. What should you do?
o: Tell them politely you'd rather help them understand it
Tell the teacher at once without saying anything to them first
questions.why: Offering to help solves the problem and keeps things fair.

questions.q: At a family function, an older relative asks about your marks. You feel uncomfortable. What's polite?
o: Answer briefly and change the topic kindly
Make up better marks so the relative stops asking questions
questions.why: Polite short answers respect elders and your comfort.

questions.q: Your friend apologises after a fight. What's a good response?
o: Accept it and talk about how to avoid it next time
Accept it, but stay cold for a few days so they learn
questions.why: Accepting and planning ahead repairs friendships.

questions.q: In a group, someone keeps making all the decisions. What can you say?
o: "Can we hear everyone's ideas before deciding?"
Say nothing, because it's easier when one person decides
questions.why: Polite suggestions make groups fairer.

questions.q: Your class is collecting donations. What's a good way to help?
o: Help collect and organise, whatever you can give
Give the biggest amount so everyone sees you care the most
Tell others what they should give
questions.why: Helping in any way is valuable.

questions.q: Your friend is being bullied but asks you not to tell. What should you do?
o: Tell a trusted adult because their safety matters
Keep the promise, because breaking it would hurt their trust
questions.why: Safety matters more than secrets.

questions.q: You meet an elderly neighbour who seems lonely. What can you do?
o: Chat with them sometimes and offer small help
Avoid the neighbour so you don't have to make conversation
questions.why: Small visits can make a big difference.

questions.q: Two classmates aren't speaking after a fight. You're friends with both. What helps?
o: Encourage them to talk and listen to each other
Pass messages between them until they are ready to talk again
questions.why: Encouraging direct talk helps them make up.

questions.q: You notice a classmate has no partner for a project. What do you do?
o: Invite them to join your group
Wait for the teacher to sort it
questions.why: Inviting them prevents them feeling left out.

questions.q: Your friend lies to you. You feel hurt. What's the best approach?
o: Tell them how it made you feel and ask why
Stop talking to them without saying why, so they work it out
questions.why: Honest talk helps friends understand each other.

questions.q: During a match, the referee makes a wrong call against your team. What's best?
o: Accept it and keep playing well
Argue with the referee until the decision is changed
questions.why: Accepting decisions shows good sportsmanship.

questions.q: You and your sibling share a room. How can you avoid fights?
o: Agree on simple room rules together
Divide the room with tape and never cross it
questions.why: Agreeing on rules together prevents arguments.

questions.q: Someone in your class has a disability. How can you be a good classmate?
o: Treat them as a friend and ask if they want help
Help them with everything, even when they don't need help
questions.why: Respect means friendship and asking before helping.

questions.q: Your friend shares a video that makes fun of a group of people. What should you do?
o: Say you don't find it funny and don't share it

Report your friend to the police
questions.why: Not spreading hurtful content shows respect for everyone.

questions.q: You're working in pairs and your partner is much faster than you. What helps?
o: Ask them to explain their method
Ask the teacher to change partners
questions.why: Learning from a partner helps you both.

questions.q: Your friend forgot your birthday. What's the best response?
o: Tell them lightly it was your birthday
questions.why: Gentle honesty lets friends make it up to you.

questions.q: In a debate, your opponent makes a good point. What should you do?
o: Acknowledge it and respond with your own point
questions.why: Acknowledging good points shows respect and confidence.

questions.q: You've been chosen to welcome guests at an event. What makes a good impression?
o: Smile, greet them, and guide them to their seats
Talk only to people you know
questions.why: Warm greetings make guests feel welcome.

o: Plan a cheaper trip that everyone can join
Tell them to ask their parents
questions.why: Inclusive planning makes sure no one is left out.

questions.why: Cheating is unfair to everyone; telling the teacher quietly and talking to your friend is the honest way.

questions.q: A teammate made a mistake that cost you a point. What's best to say?
o: "No problem, we'll get the next one!"

questions.why: Encouraging words keep the team strong.

questions.why: Deciding together is fair and keeps the friendship.

questions.why: Listening and pointing to support helps without overstepping.
